sections.heading: C2 — Managing space and speed
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Managing space and speed — continuation first

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A06
Low light reduces distance judgment, color recognition and side vision, making unexpected road users harder to notice. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A06
Headlights help the driver see and help others see the vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A06
Clean headlights at least weekly. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A06
Use headlights when poor light or blending into gray surroundings makes the vehicle hard to see. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A06
Use headlights in rain, snow, sleet, hail, fog, smoke or smog, and use low beams in bad weather. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A06
Headlights are required when pedestrians or vehicles cannot be seen one thousand feet ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A06
Headlights must be on between sunset and sunrise. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A06
Use headlights in work zones. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A06
Weather-related continuous or intermittent windshield-wiper use requires headlights. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A06
Daytime running lamps are insufficient when headlights are required, and the taillights must also be illuminated. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A06
The handbook lists headlight-use fines starting at 25 dollars and approaching 100 dollars with associated costs. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A06
At night, dim to low beams on noticing oncoming traffic; the law requires low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 300 feet behind another vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A06
If oncoming high beams persist after a few brief flashes, look toward the road's right side until the vehicle passes. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A06
Do not keep high beams on to retaliate against another driver. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A06
Switch the inside mirror to its night setting if following headlights create uncomfortable glare. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A06
Do not drive faster than a speed that allows stopping within the road illuminated by the headlights. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A06
Low beams illuminate about 250 feet ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A06
At 55 mph, stopping requires more than 250 feet even on dry pavement. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A06
To avoid outrunning headlight visibility on a dark road at night, the handbook advises no more than 45 mph. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A06
Reduce speed on poor road surfaces and take slippery turns or curves more slowly. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A06
Pavement may be especially slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A07
Rain can bring asphalt oil to the surface, and hot weather makes that slippery-road problem worse. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A07
In cold wet weather, shaded roads can freeze sooner and dry later. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A07
Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose road grip and ride on a film of water. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A07
Hydroplaning can occur at only 35 mph in water one tenth of an inch deep. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A07
Worn tires worsen hydroplaning risk, while slower driving reduces it. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A07
When hydroplaning, keep both hands on the wheel and slowly release the accelerator; avoid hard braking or sudden turns. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A07
While hydroplaning, steer slowly only as needed to remain on the road and brake gently if braking is necessary. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A07
Snow and ice reduce traction and seriously affect steering and braking. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A07
Near 32 degrees Fahrenheit, rain or sleet can put water over ice, creating a surface more slippery than ice alone. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A07
A wet-looking road with no tire spray from other vehicles may indicate black ice. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A07
PennDOT urges clearing all snow and ice off the vehicle before travel. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A07
On wet roads, reduce speed by five to ten mph and increase the following gap to five or six seconds. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A07
On packed snow, reduce speed by half. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A07
On ice, reduce speed to a crawl. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A07
On snow- or ice-covered roads, leave about ten times the normal following space. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A07
Do not use cruise control on slippery roads because continued power can maintain wheelspin. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A07
Adjust speed to avoid meeting other vehicles at slippery shaded sections or frosty bridges. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A07
On icy or packed-snow roads, coast toward an intersection to reach it after green appears and the vehicles ahead begin moving. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A07
On a wintry uphill, leave enough distance to avoid slowing or stopping behind the leading vehicle. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A07
Select a lower gear before descending a wintry hill for better control. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0045]

sections.heading: C2 — Managing space and speed
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Managing space and speed — continuation second

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A08
Do not begin a trip when fog is so dense that you cannot see. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R43 | anchor: A08
If dense fog catches you, pull completely off the road, preferably into a parking lot, and wait for it to clear. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R44 | anchor: A08
While parked waiting out fog, keep the seat belt fastened and hazard lamps on. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R45 | anchor: A08
In fog, slow enough to stop within visible distance and check the speedometer to avoid unrecognized acceleration. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R46 | anchor: A08
In fog during day or night, use low beams and available fog lamps rather than high beams, which reflect glare back toward the driver. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R47 | anchor: A08
Before snowy travel, clear the windows, hood, trunk and roof so snow does not block your view or the following driver's windshield. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R48 | anchor: A08
Clear snow, ice and dirt from headlights, taillights and direction indicators. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R49 | anchor: A08
Before snowy driving, let the engine warm so the defroster can warm the windshield and melt remaining ice. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R50 | anchor: A08
In snow, use the wipers and keep the washer reservoir full of fluid that will not freeze. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R51 | anchor: A08
Keep the defroster on for steamed windows and follow the owner's manual for the vehicle's settings. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R52 | anchor: A08
Use low beams in snowy conditions even in daylight to make the vehicle visible. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R53 | anchor: A08
A snow squall can turn clear, dry conditions into near-zero visibility and a slick road within seconds. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R54 | anchor: A09
Monitor weather forecasts and transportation message signs for snow-squall hazards. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R55 | anchor: A09
Change travel time, route or both to avoid snow squalls, particularly high-speed interstate exposure. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R56 | anchor: A09
If a squall is approaching or known to be nearby, leave the roadway and wait for it to pass. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R57 | anchor: A09
If caught in a snow squall, slow gradually, activate hazard lights and avoid slamming the brakes. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R58 | anchor: A09
After a collision in a snow squall, remain in the vehicle whenever possible. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R59 | anchor: A09
A snow-squall warning for the travel route calls for delaying or altering travel plans. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R60 | anchor: A09
When weather requires continuous or intermittent wipers, use headlights and illuminated taillights rather than daytime running lamps alone. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R61 | anchor: A09
The handbook lists a possible 25-dollar wiper-and-headlight violation fine, with fees bringing the total toward 100 dollars. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R62 | anchor: A09
Match traffic flow while staying within the posted limit. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R63 | anchor: A09
When a highway traffic pack removes the space cushion, slowing by two or three mph can help surrounding traffic clear away. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R64 | anchor: A09
With a cyclist on the right and oncoming traffic, slow to let the oncoming vehicle pass before moving left to pass the cyclist. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R65 | anchor: A09
At an emergency scene, police stop or vehicle-recovery tow truck, move to a nonadjacent lane; if unable, slow at least 20 mph below the posted limit. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R66 | anchor: A10
Large trucks, farm equipment and horse-drawn vehicles may accelerate slowly when joining traffic. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R67 | anchor: A10
On long or steep climbs, trucks typically use flashers to warn they are moving slowly. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R68 | anchor: A10
An orange rear triangle identifies farm or horse-drawn vehicles designed for speeds of 25 mph or less. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R69 | anchor: A10
Stay well behind tractors and horse-drawn vehicles and do not sound the horn to pass. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R70 | anchor: A10
Brake lights signal slowing or stopping; if other drivers may not expect braking, quickly tap the pedal three or four times. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R71 | anchor: A10
When required to travel below 40 mph on a limited-access highway, use hazard flashers to warn following drivers. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R72 | anchor: A10
A turn signal communicates the intended turn but does not give the driver priority to make it. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R73 | anchor: A10
When driving below 35 mph, signal at least 100 feet before turning. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R74 | anchor: A10
When driving at 35 mph or faster, signal at least 300 feet before turning. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R75 | anchor: A10
Use hand signals if the vehicle's turn indicators fail. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R76 | anchor: A10
The manual's hand-signal chart covers three maneuvers when turn indicators fail: a left turn, slowing or stopping, and a right turn [A10].
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R77 | anchor: A10
A child starting to run into the street is given as an example of sounding the horn when a pedestrian may not see your vehicle [A10].
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R78 | anchor: A10
When an oncoming vehicle and a bicyclist ahead coincide, handle one condition at a time by slowing behind the cyclist until oncoming traffic passes [A10].
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R79 | anchor: A10
For a highway breakdown, signal and pull off carefully, park well clear where others can see, switch on hazards and raise the hood. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R80 | anchor: A10
Use the horn when a pedestrian or driver may not see you or a vehicle appears about to strike you. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R81 | anchor: A10
If vehicle control is lost, sound the horn to warn other drivers. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R82 | anchor: A10
When passing a cyclist after oncoming traffic has cleared, leave at least four feet of passing space. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0048]
